name: TT-Metal Flash-Decode: split the KV cache across Tensix cores, reduce over the NoC
arithmetic_intensity: Decode attention reads the whole KV cache for one query token, so bytes moved grow with sequence length while the matmul is a single query row against that cache. The prefill kernel's own report finds the fused op is not fully bandwidth-bound — BFP8 is only moderately faster than BF16, not the 2x the halved datum size would give — but decode has far less arithmetic per byte read, so the split is a bandwidth play: more cores reading different KV chunks at once, then a reduction of the partial softmax statistics.
scales_with: kv sequence length (the dimension the kernel splits across cores)
batch size (one axis of the parallelization; a position of -1 skips that batch index)
number of KV heads (MQA only: the kernel does not parallelize over query heads)
k_chunk_size (unpaged default is min(512, the largest power-of-two divisor of the sequence length); paged decode defaults to 32 when no program config is set)

hardware_parameters.effect: The kernel exists to put more cores onto one KV cache read. The prefill report's evidence that the fused op is only partly bandwidth-bound is the BFP8-versus-BF16 gap being well under 2x; decode reads the same cache with one query row, so bandwidth is the tighter constraint and the split is what raises the number of cores issuing DRAM reads.
hardware_parameters.magnitude: BFP8 datum is about half a BF16 datum; the measured speedup of BFP8 over BF16 is moderate, not 2x (prefill op, vendor's own report)

hardware_parameters.effect: Each Tensix core's L1 holds the Q, K and V chunks it is working on, double-buffered so the reader fills the next chunk while compute consumes the current one. The chunk size is bounded by that L1, which is why the kernel takes an explicit k_chunk_size rather than streaming the whole sequence through one core.

workarounds: Parallelize over batch and over the KV sequence, not over query heads: the decode op only supports multi-query attention, so a grouped-query model has to be lowered to one KV head per group before this kernel applies
Keep the K chunk a power of two. Unpaged decode defaults to min(512, the largest power-of-two divisor of the sequence length), and paged decode falls back to 32 when no program config is supplied
Pass cur_pos as -1 for a batch slot that has no work rather than launching a shorter program; the kernel skips that index

On the prefill side, do not write a fused kernel until L1 sharding stops being enough: a chain of ops whose inputs and outputs all live in per-core L1 already avoids the DRAM round trip, and the fused op is only worth it when the algorithm itself changes
notes: Two sources, two kernels, one conclusion. The 2024-09-04 Wormhole FlashAttention report ([[papers/tt-metal-flashattention-wormhole]]) covers the prefill op: Q is split across cores, KV is chunked, the online softmax stays in L1, and the fused op beats the stack's own DRAM-spilling softmax attention by 20x on average (9x to 44x) at a fixed 16k tokens, hidden dim 2048, head dims 64/128/256. The current decode op, documented on the TT-NN SDPA decode page as read 2026-10-17, is the inference-relevant half: it is Flash-Decode, it splits the KV sequence across cores, and it only handles multi-query attention on a single token. The reduction of partial results across the cores that share one head is a tree over the on-chip network, and the compute kernel on main caps it at six rounds (MAX_TREE_REDUCTION_ROUNDS is 6 in sdpa_flash_decode.cpp). That cap is the practical limit on how finely one head's KV can be split before the reduction depth runs out; it is read from the kernel source, which is not separately sourced here, so treat the number six as a code fact rather than a measured limit. What the report explicitly leaves on the table, and what a hand-written kernel can still take, is multicasting one K and V head to every core holding a query head from the same group. The report names that as the way to cut DRAM traffic for multi-query attention, and the decode kernel has still not generalized past MQA. Vendor numbers throughout; the 20x is against Tenstorrent's own baseline, not against a GPU FlashAttention.
